From ugly to iconic

Record sales, shaky stock: how a 250-year-old Birkenstock sandal became a fashion icon, and why Wall Street still isn’t sure the cool will last.

BIRK $37.32 ▼ vs. $46 IPO FY2025 sales €2.1B ▲ 16% 250 years of footbeds Worn by hippies, Steve Jobs and Barbie
The storyBasicsPastPresentFuture
THE STORY

Three things to remember

1

It’s a footbed

Cork, suede and a shape copied from your foot. The shoe barely changed in 250 years.

2

Fashion made it cool

Hippies, then Céline, Dior and Barbie, with almost no advertising. Sales nearly tripled.

3

Wall Street doubts it

The share price is below its $46 IPO price. The puzzle: stay special while growing.

FUTURE

The plan to 2028, and our two ideas

13–15%growth a year, on purpose not faster
+€1Bextra sales by 2028
2× AsiaAsia-Pacific sales doubled
400+stores incl. partners, from 245
Gen Zwon in shops, where they touch it first
Our idea 1

Resole, don’t replace

A repair corner in every Birkenstock store. A cheap copy can’t be fixed; a Birkenstock can. It proves the quality and beats dupes without a courtroom.

Our idea 2

A QR code in every box

Most young fans buy at other shops, so Birkenstock never meets them. A quick scan signs them up for the club, whose members spend about 25% more.
